group: validate(JsonNode) - basic delegation and error handling

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: Passing a null JsonNode should result in a NullPointerException because the method delegates to validate(rootNode, OutputFormat.DEFAULT) which expects a non‑null node.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: A JSON document that fully satisfies the schema (e.g., required string and integer properties) should produce an empty set of validation messages.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing type‑mismatch messages for 'name' and 'age'
cases.description: When the JSON contains values of the wrong type, the validator should return messages indicating the type mismatches.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a required‑property missing message for 'name'
cases.description: If a required property defined in the schema is missing, the validator must report a validation message for the missing property.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage> (reference resolved successfully)
cases.description: A schema that contains a $ref to a valid definition should resolve the reference and validate successfully, resulting in no validation messages.

cases.expected: ValidationMessage indicating unresolved $ref error
cases.description: When a $ref points to a non‑existent definition, the validator should report an unresolved reference validation message.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage> (recursive anchor handled without infinite recursion)
cases.description: A schema that declares a recursive anchor and references itself should be processed without causing a stack overflow, yielding no validation errors for a conforming instance.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> if the instance violates the recursive definition (e.g., missing required fields)
cases.description: When the instance does not satisfy the recursively anchored schema, validation messages should be produced, confirming that recursion is correctly evaluated.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a message that the instance does not match a false schema
cases.description: When the schema is the boolean literal `false`, every instance must produce a validation error regardless of its content.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: When the schema is the boolean literal `true`, any instance (including JSON null) should be considered valid and return an empty set.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: A value that matches one of the enumerated options should pass validation.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing an enum‑mismatch message
cases.description: A value not present in the enum list must generate a validation error.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The instance exactly equals the const value, so validation succeeds.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a const‑mismatch message
cases.description: A value differing from the const definition must be reported as invalid.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: An integer within the inclusive minimum and maximum bounds validates successfully.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a minimum‑violation message
cases.description: A value lower than the defined minimum must produce a validation error.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a maximum‑violation message
cases.description: A number greater than the maximum limit should be flagged.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a multipleOf‑violation message
cases.description: An integer not divisible by the specified multipleOf must generate a validation message.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: An array whose length satisfies both minItems and maxItems passes validation.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a minItems‑violation message
cases.description: An array shorter than minItems must be reported as invalid.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a maxItems‑violation message
cases.description: An array longer than maxItems should trigger a validation error.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a uniqueItems‑violation message
cases.description: Duplicate items in an array when uniqueItems is true must be flagged.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing an item‑type‑mismatch message for index 1
cases.description: When a single schema is provided for items, each element must conform; a non‑integer element should generate a message indicating the offending index.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The instance matches exactly one subschema (the string enum), satisfying oneOf.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The integer matches exactly one of the subschemas, so oneOf validation succeeds.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a oneOf‑violation message
cases.description: The instance matches both subschemas, violating the exactly‑one requirement of oneOf.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The instance satisfies at least one subschema (the pattern), so anyOf validation passes.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The instance meets all subschemas in an allOf definition, thus validation succeeds.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: When the `if` condition matches, the `then` schema is applied; the instance satisfies the `then` constraints.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a type‑mismatch for 'value' (expected string)
cases.description: The `if` condition does not match, so the `else` schema is applied; the instance violates the `else` type requirement.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: An object containing only defined properties passes when additionalProperties is false.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing an additionalProperties violation for 'extra'
cases.description: An object with an undefined property must be reported when additionalProperties is false.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The $ref contains a URL‑encoded fragment (`%2F` for `/`). The validator must decode the fragment and resolve the definition correctly.

cases.expected: ValidationMessage indicating unresolved $ref error
cases.description: A URL‑encoded $ref that points to a non‑existent definition should result in an unresolved reference validation message.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: When the schema type includes `null`, a JSON null instance must be accepted.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: A non‑null value that matches one of the allowed types (string) also passes.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a type‑mismatch message
cases.description: A value of a type not listed (number) must be reported as invalid.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: An empty schema imposes no restrictions; any instance, including a string, should be considered valid.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: Even a numeric instance passes when the schema is empty.

cases.expected: empty Set<ValidationMessage>
cases.description: The instance does not match the schema inside `not`, so validation succeeds.

cases.expected: non‑empty Set<ValidationMessage> containing a not‑violation message
cases.description: An instance that matches the subschema inside `not` must be reported as invalid.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException indicating that the schema root must be an object
cases.description: The schema node is an array instead of an object; the validator should throw a JsonSchemaException during schema parsing.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException stating that the value of "type" must be a string or an array of strings
cases.description: The "type" keyword is given a numeric value, which is invalid according to the JSON Schema spec.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException indicating that $ref value must be a string
cases.description: A $ref keyword with a non‑string value should cause schema validation to fail with a JsonSchemaException.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException mentioning unrecognized keyword "unknownKeyword"
cases.description: The schema contains a keyword that the validator does not recognize, which must be reported as a schema‑definition error.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or StackOverflowError) indicating a circular $ref without a recursive anchor
cases.description: A schema that references itself directly without a $recursiveAnchor creates an infinite loop; the implementation should detect this and throw a JsonSchemaException rather than crashing.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException stating that all entries in a type array must be strings
cases.description: When "type" is an array, each element must be a valid type name; mixing a number should cause a schema‑parsing exception.

cases.expected: RuntimeException with message "customizer failure"
cases.description: If the ExecutionContextCustomizer supplied to the overloaded validate method throws an exception, the validate call should propagate that exception.

group: validate(JsonNode) - input node causing internal I/O error

cases.expected: ValidationMessage indicating format validation failure (no exception thrown)
cases.description: The "format" keyword may internally attempt to parse the string as a URI; an invalid URI should not raise an exception but produce a validation message. This case confirms that no unexpected IOException is thrown.
